branches.name: Class I and II
branches.rule: If wall ≤2 mm thin AND no septa AND attenuation −9 to 20 HU AND no calcification → Class I. If wall ≤2 mm thin AND (septa few (1–3) OR attenuation ≥70 HU OR attenuation >20 HU non‑enhancing OR attenuation 21–30 HU) AND any calcification allowed → Class II.

outputs.when: wall ≤ 2 mm thin && septa none && attenuation −9 to 20 HU && calcification none
outputs.recommendation: No follow‑up
outputs.quote: Simple cyst: Thin smooth wall, homogeneous simple fluid (−9 to 20 HU), no septa, no calcification.

outputs.when: wall ≤ 2 mm thin && (septa few (1–3) || attenuation ≥ 70 HU || attenuation > 20 HU non‑enhancing || attenuation 21–30 HU) && calcification any
outputs.recommendation: No follow‑up
outputs.quote: Bosniak II: Thin wall plus any one of: few thin enhancing septa; homogeneous hyperattenuating ≥70 HU; homogeneous non‑enhancing >20 HU; homogeneous 21–30 HU; calcification of any type is allowed.

branches.name: Class IIF
branches.rule: Assign Bosniak IIF when (1) a smooth wall is minimally thickened to 3 mm and shows enhancement, OR (2) one or more septa are minimally thickened to 3 mm and show enhancement, OR (3) there are many (≥ 4) smooth thin (≤ 2 mm) septa that enhance. All other combinations belong to different Bosniak categories.

outputs.when: no progression on imaging over five years
outputs.recommendation: Continue follow‑up for a total of five years
outputs.quote: For patients with a Bosniak IIF cyst that do not demonstrate progression on imaging, a followup of five years is suggested (CUA guideline).

branches.name: U1 and U2 benign
branches.rule: If the U‑grade is U1 or U2, the nodule is considered benign and does not require fine‑needle aspiration cytology (FNAC).

outputs.quote: U1 represents normal thyroid parenchyma, U2 a benign nodule.

branches.name: U3 indeterminate
branches.rule: If the nodule is classified as U3 (indeterminate/equivocal), then fine‑needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) is recommended.

outputs.recommendation: Perform FNAC
outputs.quote: FNAC is recommended for nodules classified as U3 or above.

branches.name: U4 and U5 suspicious or malignant
Unenhanced CT attenuation 10 HU or less
branches.rule: If the lesion is homogeneous and the unenhanced CT attenuation is ≤10 HU, the mass is considered benign and no further imaging is required.

outputs.classification: Benign adrenal adenoma (or other benign entity)
outputs.recommendation: No further imaging required
outputs.quote: If the non‑contrast CT is consistent with a benign adrenal mass (homogenous appearance and Hounsfield units (HU) ≤ 10) no further imaging is required.

branches.name: Indeterminate lesions above 20 HU or inhomogeneous
branches.rule: If the lesion has an unenhanced HU >20 or is inhomogeneous, immediate additional imaging is preferred over interval imaging when the patient has not undergone adrenalectomy.

outputs.recommendation: Perform immediate additional imaging (e.g., MRI, FDG‑PET/CT, or contrast‑enhanced CT with washout)
outputs.quote: the guideline suggests an individualized approach… an immediate imaging work‑up is preferred over an interval imaging follow‑up for indeterminate adrenal tumors that have not undergone surgical treatment

outputs.when: I1 = ">20 HU" OR I2 = "Inhomogeneous" AND patient declines surgery
outputs.recommendation: Repeat non‑contrast CT or MRI after 6–12 months
outputs.quote: If a patient chooses not to undergo adrenalectomy, one repeat non‑contrast CT or magnetic resonance imaging after 6 to 12 months is suggested

branches.name: Attenuation 11 to 20 HU
branches.rule: If attenuation is 11‑20 HU and size is <4 cm, classify as Category 1 (Benign) with no further imaging. If attenuation is 11‑20 HU and size is ≥4 cm, classify as Category 2 (Likely Benign) and schedule a non‑contrast CT follow‑up in 6–12 months.

outputs.quote: lesions measuring 11–20 HU with a size <4 cm; these require no further imaging (Category 1 – Benign).

outputs.recommendation: non‑contrast CT follow‑up in 6–12 months
outputs.quote: lesions measuring 11–20 HU and ≥4 cm ... a single non‑contrast CT follow‑up at 6–12 months is appropriate (Category 2 – Likely Benign).

outputs.recommendation: No routine follow‑up CT at 6–12 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months
outputs.quote: No routine follow-up CT at 6–12 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months

outputs.recommendation: CT at 6–12 months, then CT at 18–24 months
outputs.quote: CT at 6–12 months, then CT at 18–24 months

branches.name: Solid nodules, multiple
branches.rule: Use the most suspicious nodule’s size and the patient’s risk category to select the management column (low‑risk or high‑risk) from the multiple solid nodule table.

outputs.when: risk = Low risk AND size = 6–8 mm
outputs.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months
outputs.quote: Low risk → CT at 3–6 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months

outputs.when: risk = High risk AND size = <6 mm
outputs.recommendation: Optional CT at 12 months
outputs.quote: High risk → Optional CT at 12 months

outputs.when: risk = High risk AND size = 6–8 mm
outputs.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months, then at 18–24 months
outputs.quote: High risk → CT at 3–6 months, then at 18–24 months

outputs.when: risk = High risk AND size = >8 mm
outputs.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months, then at 18–24 months
outputs.quote: High risk → CT at 3–6 months, then at 18–24 months

branches.name: Subsolid nodule, part-solid
branches.rule: If size < 6 mm → no routine follow‑up. If size ≥ 6 mm and solid component < 6 mm → obtain CT at 3–6 months to confirm persistence, then repeat annually for a minimum of 5 years. If size ≥ 6 mm and solid component ≥ 6 mm → CT at 3–6 months and if suspicious consider PET/CT, biopsy or resection.

outputs.recommendation: No routine follow‑up
outputs.quote: For solitary part‑solid nodules smaller than 6 mm, no routine follow‑up is recommended (1C).

outputs.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months, then annually for 5 years
outputs.quote: For solitary part‑solid nodules 6 mm or larger with a solid component less than 6 mm in diameter, follow up is recommended at 3‑6 months and then annually for minimum of 5 years.

outputs.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months; if suspicious, consider PET/CT, biopsy or resection
outputs.quote: For solitary part‑solid nodules with a solid component 6 mm or larger, a short‑term follow‑up CT scan at 3‑6 months should be considered. For nodules with ... ... PET ... resection (1B).

branches.name: Subsolid nodule, pure ground-glass
branches.rule: If size is <6 mm, no follow‑up CT is required. If size is ≥6 mm, obtain an initial follow‑up CT within 6–12 months to confirm persistence; if the nodule remains persistent and unchanged, perform surveillance CT every 2 years for up to 5 years.

outputs.recommendation: no follow‑up surveillance CT
outputs.quote: Solitary, smaller pure GGNs (<6 mm) require no follow‑up surveillance CT.

outputs.recommendation: initial follow‑up CT within 6–12 months to determine persistence, then surveillance CT every 2 years until 5 years if persistent and unchanged
outputs.quote: Solitary, larger pure GGNs (≥6 mm) require initial follow‑up surveillance CT within 6–12 months to determine persistence, followed by surveillance CT every 2 years until 5 years if they remain persistent and unchanged.

branches.name: Subsolid nodules, multiple
branches.rule: If size is <6 mm, obtain CT at 3–6 months; if unchanged, low‑risk patients may stop, while high‑risk patients consider additional CT at 2 years and 4 years. If size is ≥6 mm, obtain CT at 3–6 months and then manage according to the most suspicious nodule among the multiple lesions, without a fixed interval specified.

outputs.recommendation: CT in 3 to 6 months; if unchanged, consider CT at 2 and 4 years
outputs.quote: CT in 3 to 6 months. If unchanged, consider CT at 2 and 4 years.

outputs.recommendation: CT in 3 to 6 months, then management based on the most suspicious nodule(s)
outputs.quote: CT in 3 to 6 months. Then management based on most suspicious nodule(s).

outputs.when: I1='definite absence' AND I2='none' AND I3='none' AND I4='none'
outputs.quote: grade 0 (none): definite absence of x‑ray changes of osteoarthritis

branches.name: LR-3 intermediate
branches.rule: Assign LR‑3 when any of the following conditions are met: (1) size < 20 mm, APHE = No APHE, and major_cnt = 0 or 1; (2) size ≥ 20 mm, APHE = No APHE, and major_cnt = 0; or (3) size < 20 mm, APHE = Non‑rim APHE, and major_cnt = 0. All thresholds and size bands are taken exactly as stated in the source.

outputs.when: size < 20 mm AND aphe = No APHE AND major_cnt = 0 or 1
outputs.quote: When the nodule diameter is < 20 mm, no arterial phase enhancement (APHE), and no or only one major features (enhancing “capsule”, nonperipheral “washout”, threshold growth);

outputs.when: size ≥ 20 mm AND aphe = No APHE AND major_cnt = 0
outputs.quote: When the nodule diameter is ≥ 20 mm, no APHE, and no other major features;

outputs.when: size < 20 mm AND aphe = Non‑rim APHE AND major_cnt = 0
outputs.quote: When the nodule diameter is < 20 mm, nonrim APHE, and no other major features.

branches.name: LR-4 probably HCC
branches.rule: Assign LR‑4 (probably HCC) when there is no arterial phase hyperenhancement, the lesion is <20 mm with two or more of washout, capsule, and threshold growth, or the lesion is ≥20 mm (size criterion alone suffices).

outputs.when: aphe = No AND size = <20 mm AND (washout = Yes + capsule = Yes) OR (washout = Yes + threshold_growth = Yes) OR (capsule = Yes + threshold_growth = Yes)
outputs.quote: LR‑4 (probably HCC) – no arterial phase hyperenhancement; <20 mm with two or more of non‑peripheral washout, enhancing capsule, threshold growth; ≥20 mm.

branches.name: LR-M
branches.rule: If any one of the listed LR‑M imaging features (rim APHE, peripheral washout, delayed central enhancement, targetoid restriction, targetoid TP/HBP appearance, infiltrative appearance, marked diffusion restriction, or necrosis/severe ischemia) is present, the observation is categorized as LR‑M.

outputs.quote: LR‑M is defined as observations that are probably or definitely malignant but not specific for HCC…any hepatic observation showing only one targetoid imaging feature can be categorized into LR‑M.

branches.name: O-RADS 3 low risk
branches.rule: Assign O‑RADS 3 (low risk) when any of the following conditions are met: (1) typical benign ovarian lesion AND size ≥ 10 cm; (2) unilocular or bilocular cyst AND size > 10 cm (simple or non‑simple); (3) multilocular cyst AND size < 10 cm AND inner wall smooth AND color score 1‑3; (4) solid lesion AND smooth outer contour AND (color score 1 OR (color score 2‑3 AND shadowing present)); (5) unilocular irregular cyst of any size.

outputs.when: Any of the criteria listed in the rule are satisfied
outputs.recommendation: 6‑month follow‑up ultrasound if not excised, or referral to a gynecologist with ultrasound specialist or MRI
outputs.quote: Low risk of malignancy (1% to <10%) - if not surgically excised then 6-month follow-up ultrasound can be performed, or if solid referral gynecologist with ultrasound specialist or MRI.

branches.name: O-RADS 4 intermediate risk
branches.rule: If the lesion is O‑RADS 4A and CA125 < 35 U/ml, classify as benign; if the lesion is O‑RADS 4A and CA125 ≥ 35 U/ml, or if the lesion is O‑RADS 4B (any CA125), or if the lesion is O‑RADS 5, classify as malignant.

outputs.quote: Lesions identified as category 1, 2, 3, or 4A with a CA125 level below 35 U/ml were classified as benign.
Lesions identified as category 4A with a CA125 level more than or equal to 35 U/ml ... were classified as malignant.
... lesions with a category of 4B ... were classified as malignant.
